title: Network People Services Technologies Ltd - 544396 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated income rose about 50% YoY to Rs 72.95 crore, a record quarter, with PAT of Rs 13.21 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 consolidated income of about Rs 72.95 crore, up roughly 50% YoY from Rs 48.68 crore and about 19-20% QoQ from Rs 61.42 crore. EBITDA was about Rs 16 crore (up 17% YoY, 15% QoQ) and PAT rose to Rs 13.21 crore. H1 FY27 income was about Rs 134 crore (up about 60% from Rs 83 crore), with EPS of 11.63. Management said H1 was execution-heavy and H2 should show growth from new POs, a Sri Lanka telecom deal, a domestic bank-in-a-box LOI and global RFPs, while the company kept its FY27 guidance unchanged.

segments.name: TSP (Third-party service provider / bank-in-a-box, UPI, licence)
segments.commentary: Now about 80-85% of business per management, up from 15-20% two years ago. Management declined to split revenue by UPI switch, IMPS or bank-in-a-box, saying the products are interlinked.

segments.name: PPaaS
segments.commentary: Named as a separate structure alongside TSP and RegTech; no revenue figure disclosed. Credit-on-UPI solution is live but has seen no client revenue traction yet.

segments.name: RegTech
segments.commentary: Won first DPDP order from a private sector bank and first digital currency order in Q2; no value disclosed.

segments.name: International / Dubai subsidiary
segments.commentary: Cost of goods sold of Rs 28 crore in Q2, of which Rs 18 crore sits in the subsidiary, which earned lower margins. Orders are turnkey, multi-client, and include licences and OEM products.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: management reiterated 60-70% growth; an analyst cited full-year revenue guidance of Rs 342 crore, implying Rs 216-226 crore in H2 (analyst's figure, not confirmed by management).
H1 described as slower due to execution; H2 expected to show growth from completions, new POs and closed global deals.
EBITDA margin expected to rise gradually; next quarter to be better than Q2 but near-term pressure from acquiring new customers in new geographies.
FY27 EBITDA margin targeted around 25%; FY28 expected around 27-28%.
Sri Lanka telecom deal: execution starts Q4 FY27; contribution from FY28, with larger numbers in FY29-30; five-year term; multi-million-dollar value, not quantified.
Bank-in-a-box LOI (central, 300+ banks): nine-month execution; revenue from Q4 or Q1; value described as 10-digit rupees; five-year direct deal term.
International pipeline of 5-15 opportunities; some results expected in Q3-Q4 FY27 and larger in FY28.
Acquisition: deal not closed; management expects to announce between now and next quarter, funded from existing cash, with international targets prioritised.
capex_capacity: Over 350 people working on the organisation, per management.
Management said it has invested in AI productivity tools across departments and targets about 40% productivity improvement this year, with deliveries by March.
Management said AI is not targeted at reducing operating cost; the aim is productivity.
New subsidiary formed in Dubai to serve global orders.
Bank-in-a-box concept launched about a year ago (Feb), went live in Feb; compliance-in-a-box being added with DPDP and compliance products.
demand_pricing: Sri Lanka telecom deal: three deals under one opportunity; combines per-transaction and licence models; per-transaction revenue said to be about 15x India levels; revenue-sharing structure.
Management said it is in active discussions in more than 10 countries.
Domestic credit-on-UPI product: live for banks, PPIs and NBFCs, but no client traction yet; banks slow to adopt the revenue model.
UPI MDR change: originally due 16 October, now postponed; management gave no quantified impact and said the new date is not set, with a possible post-festive-season timeline.
Management said the company is not exposed to AI-driven reverse engineering because its products are custom-built for specific regulatory processes.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue will the Sri Lanka telecom deal contribute, and when will services start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify the value. It said execution started, services start in Q4 FY27, and contribution is expected in FY28 with bigger numbers in FY29-30 over five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 guidance of about Rs 216-226 crore achievable, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was planned as slower, with H2 driven by execution completions, new POs and global deals; guidance was unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time vs recurring split?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Aggarwal said SaaS is about 20-25% and licence about 75-80% of Q2 revenue; one-time is below 50% and recurring above 50%, with AMC and change requests within licence.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the HSM order and the Qynx subsidiary order at lower margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiary took turnkey orders to build credentials and footprint, comprising licences and OEM products across multiple clients; HSM is a core UPI and bank-in-a-box component that the company now sells.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Aggarwal said EBITDA is currently around 24% with a FY27 target of about 25%, and FY28 could reach 27-28%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the acquisition funded from preferential issue proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is close to a few deals, with international targets first and a possible domestic consolidation later; the deal size is not finalised and existing funds will be used.

risks_watch: H2 delivery: H1 is described as execution-heavy, and the H2 ramp is needed to reach guidance.
EBITDA margin dipped in H1 versus the prior half; management expects gradual recovery.
Customer-level concentration and credit terms on the Sri Lanka and bank-in-a-box deals (government-linked nature was denied; receivable structure not disclosed).
UPI MDR changes: impact unquantified and timing postponed.
Credit-on-UPI adoption by banks has not yet produced revenue.
Acquisition terms, size and timing not yet disclosed.
Revenue split by product not disclosed; management declined to verticalise.
Subsidiary margins are below group level; watch for margin improvement as orders scale.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H2 and the international pipeline, but evasive on quantification: management declined to size the Sri Lanka deal, the bank-in-a-box value, the acquisition cost and the UPI MDR impact, citing competition and timing. Tone was more cautious on margins and near-term execution.

So, that is the model we are going right now.

growth.why: Management reiterated 60-70% FY27 growth (analyst cites Rs 342 cr, implying Rs 216-226 cr H2 vs Rs 134 cr H1), backed by new POs, a Sri Lanka telecom deal (execution from Q4 FY27), a bank-in-a-box LOI (revenue from Q4/Q1) and global RFPs, but no capacity additions and H2 needs a steep step-up with several deals not yet quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin is about 24% now against a FY27 target of about 25% and FY28 of 27-28%, though H1 margin dipped versus the prior half and subsidiary orders run at lower margin (Rs 18 cr of Rs 28 cr COGS in Q2).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions were discussed; the only new units are a Dubai subsidiary and bank-in-a-box, which are commissioned, and 350+ people are already in place.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated 60-70% FY27 growth; the analyst's Rs 342 cr implies Rs 216-226 cr in H2 against Rs 134 cr in H1, a steep step-up backed by new POs, the Sri Lanka deal (execution Q4 FY27) and the bank-in-a-box LOI (revenue Q4/Q1).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the acquisition (funded from existing cash, announcement expected by next quarter) is not capex and its size is undisclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was held unchanged and H2 must ramp steeply, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue of Rs 134 cr must roughly double-plus in H2 to reach the analyst's Rs 216-226 cr, several deals are unquantified, and the UPI MDR impact is unknown.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Compliance-in-a-box is being added to bank-in-a-box, DPDP and compliance products are rolling out, and the Sri Lanka and bank-in-a-box deals are slated to start Q4 FY27 with first revenue.

rows.label: Sri Lanka telecom deal execution
rows.why: Execution starts Q4 FY27, contribution from FY28 with bigger numbers in FY29-30 on a five-year term, though value is unquantified.

rows.label: International pipeline 5-15 opportunities
rows.why: Management is in active discussions in more than 10 countries and expects some results in Q3-Q4 FY27, with no numbers disclosed.

rows.label: Acquisition funded from cash
rows.why: Management expects to announce a deal between now and next quarter, funded from existing cash with international targets prioritised, though size and terms are undisclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 execution, the Sri Lanka deal and the international pipeline but cautious on margins and evasive on sizing the Sri Lanka deal, bank-in-a-box value, acquisition cost and UPI MDR impact; analysts probed H2 achievability and the margin path.

quality.why: Consolidated income rose about 50% YoY to Rs 72.95 crore, but the brief does not say whether volume, price or mix drove it, gives no volume figure, and names no one-off items; the one-time share (under 50% of revenue) is a revenue-type split, not a growth driver, and the acquisition is not yet closed, so no consolidation effect is stated.
